doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: 'No Greater Love' and the plunger mute
summary: They listen to his recording of 'No Greater Love', which sounds like two trumpeters, and he explains he used a plunger as a Harmon-like mute.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Growl, plunger and derby: the trumpet mute tradition

blocks.x: I wanted to play a piece and talk about improvising if we could. “No Greater Love.”
First of all it sounds like two trumpet players.
That’s exactly what I had in mind, too. It’s like a put on but you know, you’re kidding with yourself, like it’s two different guys.
What kind of mute was that?

It’s a toilet plunger, and it has a hole in the end. It has a hole in it so as you push it tight against the bell it sounds like a Harmon mute, that’s why the lighter sounds. It sounds almost like a Harmon mute. That’s why I could get away with that.
